run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T11:24:37Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is a downstream symptom of the ad service no longer serving GetAds. frontend-proxy's own spans show 1041.78 error spans in 10:24:37–11:36:02Z (528.00 on server span 'ingress', 513.78 on client span 'router frontend egress'), against a near-zero baseline until ~11:25Z and a 7.9–8.6% error ratio afterwards. Every frontend error span in the window belongs to the /api/data → grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds path, and frontend's GetAds client spans flip from ~110 successes/min with no errors to 0 successes and 90–136 errors/min from the 11:25–11:26Z minute. On the ad side, server spans for oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and all other ad operations fall to zero after the 11:24:00–11:25:00Z bucket, while the pod object records that its only container was OOMKilled (exit 137) at 11:24:06Z and restarted at 11:24:07Z — about 30 s before the alert start. The replacement container has kept running (restartCount 1) with memory climbing back toward its 450Mi limit and sharply higher CPU-throttled-period counts, but it produced no spans, and its post-restart logs are not retrievable, so the exact reason it stopped accepting/serving requests is unresolved. Failures are immediate (85% of incident GetAds error spans are ≤2 ms), not long timeouts, and other frontend dependencies (product catalog, cart, checkout, recommendation) show no errors, which argues against a cluster-wide or network-wide problem.

claims.text: frontend-proxy recorded 1041.78 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans versus 46967.63 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans over 10:24:37–11:36:02Z; the errors sit entirely on its two operations: server span 'ingress' 528.00 errors and client span 'router frontend egress' 513.78 errors (the two operations listed for this service are 'ingress' span_kind=server and 'router frontend egress' span_kind=client).

frontend-proxy error spans were near zero before ~11:25Z and jumped afterwards: 5-minute error increases were 0–5.56 for the windows ending 11:01:37Z–11:25:37Z, then 251.11 (window ending 11:27:37Z), 461.11, 486.67, 587.50 and 381.08 for the later windows.

frontend-proxy's error-to-span ratio was 0.00056, 0.00029 and 0.00075 in the 5-minute windows ending 11:15:00Z, 11:20:00Z and 11:25:00Z, and 0.0791 and 0.0857 in the windows ending 11:30:00Z and 11:35:00Z.

All 2052.34 frontend error spans in the window belong to the /api/data → GetAds path: 'GET' 508.71, 'GET /api/data' 508.71, 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' 508.83, 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' 508.83 and 'tcp.connect' 17.27; every other frontend operation (product, cart, checkout, recommendations, DNS) shows 0 error spans.

frontend's GetAds client spans switched from success to failure: 0 errors in the 1-minute samples from 11:16Z through 11:25Z with ~102–120 UNSET/min, then 122 errors with 8 UNSET in 11:25:00–11:26:00Z, and 100/90/136/118/102/120/118 errors with 0 UNSET in later samples; frontend's 'GET /api/data' error spans follow the same onset (0 until 11:25Z, then 100 and 118/120).

ad's own spans stop entirely: 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' was 100–130 per minute until the 11:24:00–11:25:00Z bucket (80) and 0 in every later bucket; internal 'getAdsByCategory'/'getRandomAds' and the flagd client spans likewise fall to 0 from the 11:26:00Z sample onward.

Pod ad-554b849958-fcl25, container 'ad' (deployment ad, ReplicaSet ad-554b849958): lastState.terminated reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-15T11:24:06Z; restartCount 1; current state running startedAt 2026-11-15T11:24:07Z; pod Ready=True since 11:24:07Z, and the container defines no livenessProbe, readinessProbe or startupProbe.

The ad pod's events show the same container being restarted ('Pulled', 'Created container: ad', 'Started container ad', each count 2) at 11:24:06–11:24:07Z; the pod name and its owner ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 are unchanged, i.e. a container restart of the existing pod rather than a controller replacement.
The ad deployment reports 1 desired replica, 1 ready and 1 available, container limits cpu=50m / memory=450Mi (requests 10m / 225Mi) on image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad.

ad container memory from cAdvisor: the killed container's working set ran ~301.6MB (10:59:37Z) to ~309.8MB (11:22–11:24Z) with container max_usage 420.4MB, and the pod-slice max_usage reaches 471,859,200 bytes (450Mi); the replacement container starts at 57.5MB (11:24:37Z), rises to ~315.1MB (11:32:37Z) and reaches max_usage 378.3MB (11:33:37Z).

ad container CPU throttling rose after the restart: container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total increased ~153.7–420.7 per 5 minutes for windows ending 10:59:37Z–11:20:37Z, then 1331.9 (11:24:37Z), 5973.6 (11:29:37Z) and 4111.0 (11:34:37Z), while container_cpu_cfs_periods_total rose from ~241–1508 to ~3000 and ~2064 per 5 minutes.

The failing GetAds client spans are fast rather than slow: of 521.99 error spans in 11:25:02–11:36:02Z, 445.93 (85%) are ≤2 ms and 471.98 (90%) ≤10 ms, compared with baseline successful GetAds spans (1398.05 in 10:34–11:24Z) where 334.05 (24%) were ≤2 ms, 1016.20 (73%) ≤10 ms and 1324.14 (95%) ≤200 ms.

Only two pods in otel-demo have restarts: ad-554b849958-fcl25 (container ad, OOMKilled, finished 11:24:06Z, restartCount 1) and fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-wbm7f (container fraud-detection, OOMKilled, finished 11:01:38Z, restartCount 1); frontend and frontend-proxy containers show restartCount 0 with no last termination.

In the same window the only ad error spans are flagd client spans ('flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 2.04 errors; ad's 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' spans carry no error status), while flagd serves cart's 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean' 1331.17 calls with 0 errors; recommendation shows 4.06 and fraud-detection 1.03 flagd EventStream errors.

The Jaeger samples returned for this window are timestamped 10:59:35–10:59:45Z (data_as_of 2026-11-15T10:59:45.310636+00:00) and are all successful HTTP 200 spans; the only error trace retrieved (load-generator 'user_browse_product' → load-generator 'GET' 503 → frontend-proxy 'ingress' 503 → 'router frontend egress' error with http.status_code 0) is from 10:59:35.13Z, i.e. before the escalation.

Other frontend dependencies show no errors in the window, arguing against a cluster-wide or frontend-wide fault: grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 20368.36 UNSET / 0 error, CartService/GetCart 5825.63/0, CartService/AddItem 3910.16/0, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 1331.48/0, RecommendationService/ListRecommendations 1878.91/0, and the /api/products, /api/cart, /api/checkout, /api/recommendations routes carry 0 error spans.

Service-level error counts over the whole window are dominated by frontend (2052.34) and frontend-proxy (1041.78), with only tiny series elsewhere: recommendation 4.06, ad 2.04, fraud-detection 1.03, and 0 for accounting, checkout and payment.
Node-level memory pressure is not supported as the cause: all five nodes report MemoryPressure=False (and DiskPressure/PIDPressure=False, Ready=True).

ad's Ready/available state does not establish that it was serving: the container has no readiness probe (nor liveness/startup probe), so Ready=True from 11:24:07Z only reflects that the process was running, while its spans and reachable logs stop around 11:24–11:25Z.

fraud-detection was also OOMKilled in the window (finished 11:01:38Z, restartCount 1) but shows only 1.03 error spans in total and an error ratio of 0 in the windows ending 11:15Z/11:25Z/11:35Z (0.0024 in the window ending 11:30Z), so no observed evidence ties it to the frontend-proxy alert.

Primary explanation for the alert: ad service unavailability is the cause of the elevated frontend-proxy request error rate. ad's only container was OOMKilled at 11:24:06Z and its replacement stopped serving GetAds (ad server spans 0 from ~11:25Z), so frontend's /api/data handler fails 100% of GetAds calls and frontend-proxy records errors on 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress'. The timing matches the alert start (11:24:37Z, ~30 s after the OOM) and the first error minute (11:25:00–11:26:00Z), but the causal link between the OOM restart and the replacement container's continued non-serving is inferred from correlation, not directly observed.

Mechanism hypothesis (unresolved): the running replacement ad container is resource-constrained and possibly hung — working set climbed back to ~315MB against the 450Mi limit (max 378MB) and 5-minute throttled-period counts rose to 1332/5974/4111 versus ~150–420 before — which could explain why it accepted no GetAds requests after ~11:25Z; the available metrics cannot separate a memory leak/GC problem from CPU starvation (50m limit) or an unlogged internal hang.

Alternative hypothesis considered: an ad→flagd dependency failure stalls ad. ad emitted 2.04 error EventStream spans only during the 11:24–11:25Z restart and none afterwards, and flagd successfully served 1331.17 cart ResolveBoolean calls with no errors, so this remains unproven and does not explain 100% GetAds failure.

Rejected: a rollout, configuration change or rescheduling of ad as the trigger. The pod name ad-554b849958-fcl25 and owner ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 are unchanged, the image digest is unchanged (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo@sha256:c9d4f94…), restartCount is 1, and the only events are container 'Created'/'Started' with count 2 at 11:24:06–11:24:07Z — a container restart in place, not a controller replacement.

Rejected: frontend-proxy itself failing (restart, crash or its own fault). Its container has restartCount 0 with no last termination, its pod has been running since 10:47:08Z, and its error spans are paired ingress/egress spans of the same proxied requests (528.00 vs 513.78) while its unproxied behaviour is otherwise normal.

Investigate why the replacement ad container, alive since 11:24:07Z, stopped serving: retrieve its current and previous container logs directly (the tool's post-restart log read returned nothing), exec/describe the container for a hang or GC/CPU stall, and confirm whether it is silently crash-looping or blocked while Ready=True without a readiness probe.

Add a readiness probe to the ad container and revisit its resources: memory limit 450Mi against a working set that reached ~315MB (max 378MB) after the restart, and cpu limit 50m with a clear post-restart rise in throttled periods, are plausible contributors to both the OOM kill and the unresponsive replacement.

Review the RequestErrorRate rule definition: it fires at 'above 0' (annotation current 1.5333) while frontend-proxy already carried a non-zero baseline error ratio of 0.0003–0.0007, so a non-zero threshold or longer window is worth considering to avoid alerting on background error noise.

gaps: Jaeger returned no trace spans for the 11:20–11:36Z period (its newest returned trace data is 10:59:45Z; the later search returned no traces), so the exact gRPC status code / message of the failing GetAds calls and the HTTP status frontend returned to frontend-proxy during the incident are unknown.
Frontend application logs returned 0 lines for 10:55–11:36Z, so no application-level error text exists in the evidence for the failing /api/data handler.

The ad container's logs for 11:24:10Z–11:36:02Z returned no lines and the previous container instance was reported unavailable, so the reason the replacement container stopped serving (panic, hang, second OOM, throttling) is not observable.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule was not returned by list_prometheus_rules (status no_data), so its expression, threshold, lookback and 'for' duration could not be verified; only the alert labels/annotations (severity warning, current 1.5333) are known.

kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total and last-terminated-reason metrics are not present in this Prometheus (no_data), so the restart/termination timeline rests only on the pod object's lastState read at ~11:37Z.

ad and frontend expose only traces_span_metrics_* series; rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_count{rpc_grpc_status_code=...} for ad and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count for frontend returned no series, so no server-side gRPC status codes are available.

flagd logs (all containers) returned no lines and the networkpolicies query returned no objects with status no_data, so flagd's runtime health and the absence of a network policy could not be cited as facts.
Whether ad is still not serving and whether the alert is still firing after the 11:36:02Z window end is unknown; no data beyond the authorized window was queried.
next_steps: Fetch the ad pod's previous-instance and current logs directly from the cluster (kubectl logs --previous / current) to determine why the container running since 11:24:07Z stopped answering GetAds.
Describe/exec the ad container to check for a hung process, GC/CPU stall or second OOM, and confirm whether the process is still listening on its gRPC port.
Compare ad's memory usage growth with its 450Mi limit and its 50m CPU limit, and add a readiness probe so a non-serving ad instance is removed from the service endpoints.
Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule expression and evaluation window from the alerting configuration to confirm what 'current: 1.5333' measures.
